questions.q: How does linking a story to a real object change how much you trust it?
questions.answer: It makes it easier to trust. An object shows the story wasn't just remembered wrong, like a family keepsake that backs up a parent's story from childhood.

questions.q: After two weeks of evidence, has the way you see the Bible changed at all?
questions.answer: One honest answer: "I always believed it was God's Word, but I didn't know how much evidence shows it's real history, so I take it more seriously now."

questions.q: If a friend said the Bible is just old myths, how would you answer them?
questions.answer: I'd say archaeology keeps matching its details: coins point to King David, an inscription names Pontius Pilate, and the pool in John 5 was found just as John described.
